clips.text_en_c2: A perennial /biz/ thread poses the seemingly unanswerable question: if constrained to hold a single asset for the ensuing decade, would one elect Bitcoin or gold? Anons marshal competing arguments predicated upon digital scarcity, programmed halving cycles, and concerted central bank accumulation of the yellow metal. Tommy told me to write up another condition survey for the GI report. Factor of safety 1.2 feels too close for a permanent slope near a highway.

signal.rationale: Site engineering observation, not a trade

clips.text_en_b2: Back at the slope site this morning and the factor of safety on the critical section came back at 1.2. Although the contractor insists this is acceptable, I remain unconvinced because the margin feels razor thin for a permanent cut slope sitting right next to a highway. Tommy has asked me to put together another condition survey for the GI report, which means another evening sacrificed to paperwork instead of FE revision.
clips.text_en_c1: Back on the slope site today and the factor of safety on the critical section has come back at a sobering 1.2. The contractor is adamant that this is acceptable, though my professional instincts suggest otherwise, particularly given that the slope sits adjacent to a live highway corridor. Tommy has instructed me to draft an additional condition survey for inclusion in the geotechnical interpretive report. Once I return home, the FE manual awaits, and frankly, the prospect of opening it feels insurmountable.
clips.text_en_c2: Returning to the slope site this morning revealed a factor of safety of precisely 1.2 along the critical section, a figure the contractor dismisses as adequate whilst my own engineering instincts rebel against such complacency. For a permanent cutting adjacent to a live highway, FOS values this close to unity offer scant margin against adverse pore-water pressure or unforeseen surcharge loading. Tommy, evidently sharing my reservations, has instructed me to compile an additional condition survey for inclusion within the geotechnical interpretive report. The prospect of documenting deficiencies after a gruelling shift, only to return home to FE revision notes, suggests the evening promises little beyond fatigue and the quiet contemplation of professional inadequacy.

clips.text_zh: 夜晚返到屋企，攤開FE書睇load path。Beam到column到foundation，concrete同steel兩個code都要背。Sum Ho何生成日問我點check，答唔出真係想死。
clips.text_en_b1: Studying load path for the FE exam tonight. The beam carries the slab load, the column takes it down, and the foundation spreads it into the soil. I need to remember the sequence for both concrete ACI and steel AISC codes. My boss Sum Ho will ask tomorrow so I cannot afford to forget it again.
clips.source_hint: /biz/ tariff revenue thread, reused for load path study
clips.text_en_b2: Spent the evening hunched over the FE textbook trying to nail down load path once and for all. The sequence runs from beam down through column and finally into the foundation, spreading into the soil below. I need to keep both the ACI concrete and AISC steel provisions straight in my head, which is easier said than done. Sum Ho will almost certainly quiz me on this tomorrow, so I cannot afford to blank out again.
clips.text_en_c1: Tonight finds me hunched over the FE reference manual, meticulously tracing the load path from slab to beam, from beam to column, and ultimately from column down into the foundation strata. I must commit to memory the corresponding provisions within both the ACI concrete code and the AISC steel specification, a task that demands considerable rote effort. Sum Ho will almost certainly probe me on the sequence tomorrow morning, and failing to articulate the response correctly would be, frankly, mortifying.
clips.text_en_c2: Evening revision sessions have become an exercise in disciplined memorisation, particularly with the FE examination looming inexorably closer. The load path concept, seemingly elementary, demands rigorous internalisation: tributary loads accumulate upon the slab, transfer through the beam, descend via the column, and ultimately disperse through the foundation into the underlying strata. Both the ACI concrete provisions and the AISC steel code require fluency, given that Sum Ho will undoubtedly probe my comprehension with characteristic persistence tomorrow morning. The prospect of fumbling through such fundamental principles before a senior engineer is mortifying enough; failing to articulate the sequence would represent a humiliation from which professional redemption would prove extraordinarily difficult to extract.

clips.text_en_c1: A /g/ thread has reignited a familiar debate, arguing that frontier model development has effectively plateaued, with laboratories now resorting to elaborate narratives about self-restraint merely to keep venture capital flowing through their pipelines. The original poster is weary of such evasions. Should the plateau thesis prove accurate, my own white-collar engineering career might enjoy a longer lease than previously anticipated, which would meaningfully reshape my five-year timeline for relocating back to Florida.
clips.text_en_c2: A /g/ thread circulating this week contends that frontier model development has reached a discernible plateau, with laboratories increasingly resorting to rhetoric concerning self-restraint and alignment in order to perpetuate the venture capital largesse upon which their valuations depend. The poster, weary of such sophistry, sees through the narrative entirely. For a white-collar engineer such as myself, however, the implications are materially consequential: should genuine artificial general intelligence prove more distant than feared, my civil engineering profession might retain its relevance somewhat longer than recent prognostications suggested. Such an outcome would meaningfully recalibrate the five-year timeline I have constructed for repatriation to Florida, transforming existential anxiety into cautious optimism.

clips.text_en_c1: /pol/ is currently savouring a rare moment of triumph after Dario visibly decelerated his lab's frontier push, Altman quietly stepped aside, and Musk boarded the express. The so-called doomers are declaring a comprehensive victory on the basis that progress at the frontier has unmistakably slowed. clips.text_en_c2: Celebrations are underway on /pol/ following Dario's deceleration, Musk's belated endorsement, and Altman's apparent withdrawal from the frontier race, developments that collectively suggest the velocity of state-of-the-art model releases has measurably diminished. One fewer existential variable to dread constitutes, in the current circumstances, a modest but welcome reprieve.

clips.text_zh: /fit/有個anon問幾時先可以停bulk走去cut，由65kg skinnyfat操到80kg, bench 1 pl8, squat 90, dead 120。睇完好想跟肥仔信去gym，但我今日返工地返到散咗。
clips.text_en_b1: A /fit/ anon asks how he knows when he has bulked enough to cut. He was 65kg skinnyfat and could not even bench the 20kg bar. He lean bulked back to 80kg and now benches 1 plate, squats 90kg, and deadlifts 120kg. He can see the difference but still feels flat. Sounds like me before my next gym session with Fat Boy.
clips.text_en_b2: A /fit/ anon wants to know when he can finally switch from bulk to cut. He started at 65kg skinnyfat and could not even bench the empty 20kg bar, then lean bulked his way up to 80kg with a one plate bench, a 90kg squat, and a 120kg deadlift. Although the mirror shows progress, he still feels frustratingly flat. Reading it after a brutal shift on site, I can relate, and I am itching to train with Fat Boy.
clips.text_en_c1: A /fit/ anon has posed the perennial bulk-versus-cut dilemma, asking when the appropriate moment arrives to transition into a cut. He commenced his journey at a skeletal 65 kilograms, barely capable of pressing the empty 20-kilogram bar. Following a disciplined lean bulk, he now stands at 80 kilograms with a one-plate bench, a 90-kilogram squat, and a 120-kilogram deadlift. Progress is visible, though he still perceives a lingering flatness in his physique. The sentiment resonates, particularly given today's backbreaking shift on site.
clips.text_en_c2: A /fit/ anon recently solicited guidance on the perennial dilemma of when to terminate a bulk and initiate a cut, a question that resonates more deeply than I care to admit. His trajectory is commendable: from a 65kg skinnyfat neophyte unable to bench even the unladen 20kg barbell, he has lean-bulked to 80kg and now handles 90kg squats, 120kg deadlifts, and a single-plate bench. Despite these verifiable gains, he perceives a lingering flatness in his physique that no amount of mirror scrutiny seems to remedy. His account mirrors my own circumstances precisely, particularly after today's exhaustive shift at the construction site, wherein even the thought of accompanying Fat Boy to the gym borders on the physically unbearable.
